My original Javascript in whoaverse suggestion is simply not as powerful or useful as what is proposed in this (because of the way stuff works).

So, we could have like whoascript. So like, whoascript would have its own textarea just under the css area, and whoascript could be used in CSS and sidebar text as well, and possibly even comments (no user access - i mean stuff like highlighting certain words using whoascript).

Syntax could be somewhat like CSS, to prevent abuse. So like you could have different properties and stuff, such as

eg. selecting a comment by me

comment(author='teh_sauce_guy'){
css{
 color:#FF0000;
 }
}

And variables

[@variable-str](https://preview.voat.co/user/variable-str)('changingFill') = 'dolor';

We could also use variables in CSS and sidebar

Lorem ipsum {@changingFill} sit amet

And other stuff! 

[@variable-str](https://preview.voat.co/user/variable-str)('foo') = 'bye';
comment(author='teh_sauce_guy';count="3"){
css{
 color:#FF0000;
 }
replace("hi",@foo);
}

And it would output (pretend this is a comment by me)

 bye, I'm teh_sauce_guy

assuming it was originally "hi, I'm teh_sauce_guy".

count would refer to the 3rd comment by me in a thread

We could also have

[@variable-str](https://preview.voat.co/user/variable-str)('bar') = 'teh_sauce_guy is the best';
comment{
replace("teh_sauce_guy is the worst",@bar);
}

This would select every comment and replace worst with @bar, which is best.

Obviously this would be no easy nor realistic (considering how much other stuff that must be done) undertaking, but it's a nice thought. This is also obviously a very early idea, so many improvements will have to be made.
